areas.name: Homepage and first impression
areas.strength: Memorable travel theme, restrained layout, clear name and Doha location.
areas.reaction: I see visual ambition. I need to reach relevant product work and understand the candidate’s specialty faster.
areas.gap: A distinctive presentation takes precedence over a concrete reason to hire.
areas.placement: Fix before directing more applications to the site.
rows: P0
Strengthen
Immediate access to work
The first public visit opens the boarding-pass interaction. Skip exists, but the work remains behind the intro.
Why must I perform an unrelated task before evaluating this designer?
Show the portfolio on first load. Offer the boarding interaction as an optional experience from the page.
A new visitor reaches project summaries without scanning, waiting or finding Skip.
Design
P1
Strengthen
A specific professional promise
The headline combines Product Designer, UX Strategy and AI Enablement. The introduction uses broad claims about complex journeys and outcomes.
What kind of design problem is this person especially useful for?
Lead with product design and one evidenced specialty: Arabic/English systems or complex customer journeys. Explain AI as a working method lower down.
The opening names the role, problem domain and relevant evidence in two short sentences.
Edit
P1
Strengthen
Project evidence in the opening viewport
The aircraft window and AI-agent panel receive substantial early visual space. Projects appear lower in the page.
I see personality before I see the quality of the work.
Bring a meaningful screen and the first selected project into the opening view. Reduce the window’s vertical footprint.
At a typical laptop viewport, a project, its problem and your contribution are visible without scrolling.
Design
P1
Missing
A clear selected-work action
Resume and LinkedIn are the prominent hero links. Selected work is introduced through the timeline.
What should I open first?
Add a prominent View selected work anchor beside Resume. Link it to the first complete project summary.
The first action takes a reviewer directly to the strongest case study choices.
Edit
P1
Strengthen
AI-agent hierarchy
Interview me through my AI agent is a large panel near the top.
Do I need to talk to an agent to understand or contact the candidate?
Move the agent below selected work and label it optional. Put direct contact and your own concise introduction first.
The portfolio explains your skills and provides contact without opening the widget.
Design
P1
Missing
Credible achievement beside the promise
Measurable outcomes appears in the introduction, while project results or release status are not summarized there.
What supports the outcome claim?
Add one dated, attributed achievement or concrete delivery fact with a project link. Use a delivery fact when causal impact is unavailable.
Every headline achievement leads to supporting context and clearly distinguishes delivery from impact.
Edit
P1
Missing
A human introduction
The opening provides identity and location, but little personal explanation of how you work with teams.
Who would I be collaborating with?
Add two sentences describing your transition from marketing, design judgment and preferred collaboration. An authentic portrait is optional.
A reviewer can explain your background and how it improves your design practice.
Edit
P1
Strengthen
Evidence of original judgment
The workspace README records adaptation of another portfolio’s layout, imagery and fonts. A visitor cannot infer which decisions are yours.
Can this candidate originate a design direction as well as execute a reference?
Develop a personal layout and interaction direction around your work. Retain appropriate provenance for adapted assets and explain one original portfolio decision.
The visual identity has a clear personal rationale and adapted assets have appropriate attribution or replacement.
Design
P2
Missing
Role and working preference
Doha is visible, but the homepage does not state the opportunities or work arrangements you seek.
Is this candidate relevant to my open role and location?
Add a concise, truthful line naming the UX/UI or product-design roles and work arrangements you are open to.
Role and location fit can be understood without contacting you.
Edit
P1
Verify
First-impression comprehension
There is no visible evidence that recruiters or designers have evaluated the portfolio’s opening.
Does the memorable intro actually help me understand the candidate?
Give several relevant reviewers a short unaided visit. Ask what role you seek, which work they would open and what remains unclear.
Record recurring misunderstandings, revise the opening and repeat the same questions. Treat this as qualitative feedback.

areas.name: Project selection and navigation
areas.strength: Seven projects are curated into featured work, more case studies and community tools.
areas.reaction: The selection is manageable, but I must open several pages to judge relevance and maturity.
areas.gap: Project rows communicate titles and descriptions more clearly than contribution, status and proof.
areas.placement: Lead with three complementary cases and a small supporting-tools section.
rows: P1
Strengthen
A deliberate reading order
Andalus and Nasaq are featured. Flex and Veyra sit in a separate list.
Which project best proves suitability for my role?
For product/UX roles, lead with Andalus, Nasaq and Flex. For visual/interaction roles, bring Veyra forward once its prototype story is consistent.
Each of the first three projects proves a different skill and the order matches the target application.
Edit
P1
Missing
Useful project thumbnails
The live homepage presents compact icon-and-text rows rather than meaningful interface previews.
Can this candidate design interfaces at the level we need?
Show one readable product screen per featured project. Use a crop demonstrating interaction or hierarchy, not a logo or decorative device alone.
A reviewer can compare the interface craft of the featured projects before opening them.
Design
P1
Missing
Consistent project status labels
Project rows do not distinguish independent systems, client design work, prototypes and released products.
Am I evaluating shipped client outcomes or exploratory work?
Add truthful status labels such as Client design, Independent system, Working prototype or Released. Date the label.
Every homepage project states its maturity without implying unverified deployment or adoption.
Edit
P1
Missing
Contribution and result in project summaries
Homepage rows describe what each project does, with limited ownership or outcome context.
What did this person personally contribute?
Add a compact line with your responsibility, one decisive design change and the verified result or current validation stage.
Each project summary answers problem, contribution and evidence in a short scan.
Edit
P0
Strengthen
English access to Nasaq
The public homepage opens the Arabic case study. An English case study exists. The local language-choice page is not deployed.
I may leave before discovering the version I can read.
Link the English portfolio to the English case study or deploy an obvious English/Arabic choice. Preserve access to both versions.
A first-time English reader reaches the English case directly from the homepage.
Edit
P1
Strengthen
Stable project URLs
Several projects open inside an iframe dialog. This keeps the parent address rather than clearly representing the selected case.
Can I bookmark this case or share it with the hiring panel?
Make each project’s direct URL the normal destination, or synchronize the address and browser history with the selected case.
Copying the address while reviewing a project opens that same project in a new session.
Design
P1
Strengthen
A predictable return path
Portfolio, CV and documentation links serve different roles across project headers. The public Nasaq case header lacks a direct portfolio return.
How do I return to compare the next project?
Provide Back to portfolio in a consistent place and restore the selected-work position after returning.
A reviewer returns from every project without searching or losing their place.
Design
P2
Strengthen
Section numbering
The public homepage sequence moves from 01, 02 and 03 to 05 Experience.
Was content removed without a final review?
Renumber the visible sections consecutively or remove decorative numbering.
All visible section labels form a coherent sequence.
Edit
P2
Strengthen
Additional project curation
Six other live project pages are present but unlinked from the current selected-work list.
A large undifferentiated archive could dilute the strongest work.
Keep the seven-project curation tight. Add an optional More experiments destination only when those pages add relevant evidence.
Additional work has a clear secondary location and does not displace stronger cases.
Edit
P1
Missing
A clear next project recommendation
Some pages return home or to a CV, while Flex recommends Andalus.
Where should I look for the next relevant skill?
End each featured case with one complementary case and a one-line explanation of what it demonstrates.
A reviewer can follow a coherent three-project route without returning to a list after every case.

areas.name: Case-study structure and evidence
areas.strength: The main cases already explain design intent, tradeoffs and important limits honestly.
areas.reaction: The reasoning is promising. I need evidence of what happened when users, clients or engineers challenged it.
areas.gap: Planned validation appears more often than completed learning and documented iteration.
areas.placement: Strengthen two flagship cases deeply before expanding the portfolio.
rows: P1
Missing
An outcome-led case summary
Several cases open with brand-style headlines before a concise decision and evidence summary.
What should I learn about this designer from this case?
Add a short opening block: user problem, business constraint, your responsibility, decisive change and outcome/current status.
The central design achievement is understandable before the long narrative.
Edit
P1
Strengthen
Ownership beyond a role label
Role or scope appears in some cases, but decision authority, collaborators and handoff responsibilities are often unclear.
Which parts did you actually own?
State what you designed, what collaborators supplied and which decisions you influenced or approved. Separate team results from personal work.
A reviewer can distinguish your judgment, execution and collaborators’ contributions.
Edit
P1
Missing
Timeline and real constraints
The cases describe scope more consistently than duration, team capacity, deadlines or platform constraints.
Can you deliver within the constraints of a real team?
Add actual dates or duration, team shape and two constraints. Explain how one constraint changed the solution.
A concrete constraint is connected to a documented design decision.
Edit
P1
Strengthen
Traceable research evidence
Andalus and Veyra label hypotheses honestly. Flex explicitly says participant feedback is pending.
Can you move from a plausible assumption to evidence?
For priority cases, conduct the prepared study and publish anonymized observations, participant context and the limits of the sample.
At least one design decision traces to actual observed behavior, with the source and limits stated.
Research
P1
Missing
One complete iteration story
Final screens and rationales are stronger than documented versions, observed failure and retest.
How do you improve a design when the first solution fails?
Show the original design, the evidence of a problem, the revised design and the subsequent check.
A reader can trace one full evidence-to-change-to-recheck sequence.
Research
P1
Strengthen
Alternatives and selection criteria
Veyra compares configure-first and explore-first. Other cases offer fewer concrete rejected options.
Was this solution selected deliberately or just polished first?
Show two credible alternatives for one key decision, the criteria used and the cost of the chosen option.
A reviewer can explain why the selected option fit the constraints better.
Design
P1
Strengthen
An explicit evidence level for results
Some pages show counts of tests, components or indexed resources. Andalus separates recovery rate from incremental lift.
Are implementation counts being presented as user or business success?
Label build facts, observed usability outcomes and business outcomes separately. Add dates, denominators and sources to impact claims.
Each prominent result is unambiguous about what it measures and what it cannot establish.
Edit
P1
Missing
A collaboration decision
The portfolio emphasizes individual execution more than feedback, negotiation and team delivery.
Will this designer work constructively with product and engineering?
Include one real disagreement or scope negotiation: each perspective, your response and the resulting decision. Attribute others fairly.
The case shows a concrete example of listening, judgment and shared delivery.
Edit
P1
Strengthen
Inspectable interaction evidence
Screenshots, wireframes and several interactive studies exist, but reviewers must explore to identify the important behavior.
Can I inspect the interaction without installing or signing in?
Provide a short captioned walkthrough and an optional interactive path showing the main task plus one recovery state.
The key behavior is assessable with no external account and without guessing the task.
Design
P2
Strengthen
Specific reflection
Reflections often summarize a product philosophy or intended next step.
What did this designer learn that will improve their next project?
End with one decision you would repeat, one you would change and one unresolved question, each tied to evidence in the case.
The reflection contains a concrete lesson rather than only a slogan.

areas.name: About, CV and contact
areas.strength: Contact details and a readable CV exist. Marketing experience is connected to UX work.
areas.reaction: The commercial background is useful. I need a consistent account of experience and evidence of the research skills listed.
areas.gap: Positioning, experience claims and the route to contact can be more consistent.
areas.placement: Use this section to reduce uncertainty after the work earns interest.

Strengthen
Original titles and truthful functional focus
Experience titles combine UX focus with marketing titles.
Is the UX wording the official role or a description of the work?

Employment title and functional responsibilities are distinct and consistent across materials.

Missing
A concise transition story
Marketing experience and physics education are visible, but their connection to product design is mostly implied.
How did the candidate develop their design practice?
Add a short account of the transition, relevant learning and the projects that demonstrate current capability.
The background supports the design story without implying an invented employment history.

P1
Strengthen
Evidence for research claims

Where can I inspect research the candidate has actually conducted?

Every research claim has an example you can explain and show in an interview.

P1
Missing
Direct email on the homepage
Email appears in the CV. The homepage’s main contact route is WhatsApp, with LinkedIn and telephone links.
Can I send a routine recruitment email without using personal messaging?
Add a visible mailto link and a copy-email option beside the contact action.
A recruiter can find and use email without opening the CV or a messaging app.

P2
Missing
Working languages
Arabic/English design work is prominent, but professional language capability is not stated clearly in the reviewed CV.
Can this candidate collaborate with our team and local users?
List your working languages and accurate proficiency in the About/CV section.
Language capability is explicit and can be supported in conversation.

P1
Strengthen
CV outcomes and attribution
The CV repeats reported Andalus return and booking rates, while the case carefully limits causal interpretation.
Did the candidate cause these results or report programme performance?
Use the same source and attribution boundary in the CV as in the case. Add measured personal contributions where documented.
CV claims and case-study evidence agree about causality and ownership.

P2
Verify
Downloadable CV consistency
The site has a printable CV page and a PDF file in the workspace. The current equivalence was not verified.
Will a downloaded copy contradict what I just read?
Compare the live CV, generated PDF and application copy. Update from one authoritative version and date it.
Name, role, dates, project scope and contact match across the documents.

P1
Missing
External evidence of collaboration
There are no prominently presented client or teammate endorsements in the reviewed material.
What is it like to work with this candidate?
Add one specific, permissioned endorsement about a contribution or collaboration. State the person’s working relationship to you.
The endorsement is attributable, relevant and avoids vague praise or invented quotes.

P1
Strengthen
Interview relevance
The CV has broad lists across design, AI and marketing.
Which capabilities can the candidate demonstrate deeply today?
Prioritize skills supported by the three lead cases. Move secondary marketing tools into a short background line.
The main skills each connect to an inspectable portfolio example.

areas.name: Accessibility, performance and reliability
areas.strength: Skip links, reduced-motion handling and some native controls are present in source. Flex already identifies a contrast issue.
areas.reaction: The presentation is ambitious. I want the portfolio itself to demonstrate reliable interaction and inclusive design.
areas.gap: A complete mobile, keyboard, assistive-technology and performance audit was not established in this review.
areas.placement: Verify high-value review paths first; avoid blanket accessibility or speed claims.
rows: P1
Verify
Narrow-screen project reading
Desktop was visually inspected. Actual phone behavior was not fully tested.
Can I review this portfolio from my phone without losing content?
Check the homepage and all featured cases at narrow widths on real phones. Include screenshots, tables, sticky controls and embedded pages.
Core content and actions remain usable without accidental horizontal scrolling or obscured text.
Verification
P1
Verify
Keyboard path through the portfolio
Source includes keyboard entry and dialog controls, but a complete traversal was not performed.
Does the designer account for people who do not use a pointer?
Traverse entry, selected work, project dialogs and contact with keyboard only. Check order, visible focus, closing and restored focus.
Every review task can be completed, and returning from a dialog restores a sensible focus position.
Verification
P1
Verify
Reduced-motion experience
The source handles prefers-reduced-motion, but the combined experience across projects was not verified.
Does the story depend on motion or leave me waiting?
Enable reduced motion and inspect scanner entry, clouds, reveals, project transitions and walkthroughs.
Content is immediately available and no information requires animation to be understood.
Verification
P1
Verify
Text and control contrast
Muted text appears throughout. Flex reports white on #5070FE at 4.13:1 for normal text.
Are visual refinement and readable text being balanced?
Measure actual foreground/background pairs in both themes, including labels, disabled states and focus indicators. Fix failed combinations.
Publish a small tested-state matrix with the applicable contrast criteria, rather than an unverified compliance claim.
Verification
P1
Verify
Zoom and text resizing
Several case studies use very large editorial text and dense mock interfaces. Zoom behavior was not fully tested.
Can I read enlarged text without the page falling apart?
Check browser zoom and increased system text on main pages. Replace essential tiny screenshot text with readable captions or detail views.
Meaning and actions survive enlargement without overlap or clipped controls.
Verification
P1
Verify
Screen-reader structure
The reviewed tree exposes many mock interface details, images and decorative elements.
Can a nonvisual reviewer distinguish the case narrative from illustrative UI?
Check heading order, landmarks, link names, alternative text and mockup grouping with a screen reader. Hide purely decorative content appropriately.
A coherent reading path explains the case and identifies meaningful actions without excessive mockup noise.
Verification
P1
Verify
Initial-load performance
The entry uses a 3D scanner, fonts, motion and an external agent widget. No measured performance result was collected.
Will this page be responsive on a slower connection or older laptop?
Measure initial and returning visits on representative devices and constrained networks. Defer nonessential 3D and agent assets.
Record measured loading and responsiveness before and after changes, including the device and conditions.
Verification
P1
Verify
Third-party failure fallback
AI-agent and Figma content depend on external services. Direct Figma links exist in some cases.
Can I still evaluate the candidate when embeds fail?
Block third-party loads and verify readable screenshots, captions, direct links and ordinary contact remain.
The main review journey works when the agent or prototype embed is unavailable.
Verification
P1
Verify
Deep links and browser history
Project dialogs, hash navigation and dedicated pages use different navigation patterns.
Can I safely open, refresh, go back and share a case?
Check direct URLs, refresh, Back, Forward and new-tab opening for every featured project. Include language switches.
Each action preserves a predictable page and offers a clear return to selected work.
Verification
P2
Missing
A portfolio improvement feedback loop
Analytics code exists, but collection alone does not explain why reviewers leave.
Is this candidate evaluating the portfolio as a product?
Track meaningful project opens, contact starts and broken paths. Combine those observations with short reviewer sessions before revising.
Priorities follow observed navigation problems; time on site is not treated as proof of hiring interest.

areas.name: Andalus Cart Recovery
areas.strength: Strong cross-channel reasoning, fare-change and sold-out states, wireframes, and an honest incrementality plan.
areas.reaction: This candidate thinks beyond screens. I still cannot tell which design was implemented or what user learning changed it.
areas.gap: Reported programme rates lack denominator/date detail and do not establish design-caused improvement.
areas.placement: Lead case for UX strategy and commercially grounded product design.
rows: P1
Strengthen
Delivery and retrospective boundaries
The case shows strategy, designed return states and a future experiment. It does not clearly separate historical delivery from later exploration.
What happened in the actual engagement?
Add a dated timeline distinguishing work delivered in the role, later case-study reconstruction and planned next steps.
A reader can identify exactly what existed at each stage and what remains proposed.
Edit
P1
Strengthen
Your decision authority and team
My focus is journey strategy and UX design, with broad scope stated.
Did you lead the service decision, design the UI, or summarize a programme?
Name your responsibilities, collaborators, supplied inputs and handoff recipient. Show one decision you personally owned.
Ownership of strategy, wireframes, interface design and measurement is unambiguous.
Edit
P1
Strengthen
The three rate definitions
40%, 13–15% and 4% are attributed to programme reporting and explicitly not one funnel.
Can these figures be evaluated or compared?
Add reporting period, source, numerator, denominator and cohort definition for each rate, or explicitly state which details are unavailable.
No reader must infer a funnel or incremental uplift from unrelated rates.
Edit
P1
Missing
Actual traveler or support evidence
Exploring, coordinating and blocked are explicitly working hypotheses. Evidence collection is proposed.
Were these recovery needs observed among the agency’s customers?
Conduct interviews or analyze consented support/session evidence. Show which of the three hypotheses were supported, changed or rejected.
Each retained segment connects to actual behavior and a resulting design decision.
Research
P1
Missing
A documented existing-state comparison
A generic return journey is diagrammed, and wireframes are provided.
How does the proposal improve the agency’s actual previous experience?
Show a permissioned or anonymized original flow beside the revised flow. Label reconstructed examples and annotate repeated-entry reductions.
The baseline is identifiable and the exact change in user effort is visible.
Design
P1
Strengthen
Completed usability findings
The page lists recognition, fare-change, sold-out and cross-device tasks to test next.
Can travelers understand the uncertainty and resume successfully?
Run the prepared tasks with relevant travelers. Record task outcome, hesitation and fare/status comprehension. Include one failure-led revision.
The case shows actual observations, design changes and a focused retest without inflating small-sample findings.
Research
P1
Strengthen
Operational handoff behind the blueprint
Shared trip state, permissions, freshness, contact budget and suppression are described.
How would this survive implementation details?
Add a compact service blueprint assigning ownership of capture, identity, booking checks, contact eligibility and support exceptions.
One end-to-end scenario identifies the responsible system/team and failure fallback at each step.
Design
P1
Strengthen
A visual experiment readout
The A/B/C design is already thoughtful and correctly separates recovery from incrementality.
Can the team turn the plan into a decision?
Define eligibility, allocation, booking window, primary denominator and rollout decision. When run, publish the actual comparison with uncertainty and guardrails.
The plan is executable; any result names its period, cohort and limits. Keep it labeled planned until executed.
Research
P1
Strengthen
Multilingual and small-screen craft
The story is English while product examples use French and DZD for an Algerian context.
Does the interface work for the agency’s actual language and device needs?
Explain the supported customer languages and show one phone flow with long names, fare updates and a clear booking-status message.
Language choices follow the real audience; key comprehension states are inspectable at phone size.
Design
P1
Missing
A concrete client or team response
The reflection describes connective thinking, but offers little delivery acceptance or stakeholder feedback.
Did this work change an agreed product or operational decision?
Include a real client decision, handoff acceptance or permissioned collaborator statement and explain what it changed.
There is attributable evidence of the work’s organizational effect, even if launch metrics are unavailable.

Missing
The design-system problem
The case opens with identity and an Arabic-first idea, then shows visual foundations.

P1
Missing
Role, timeline and collaborators

What was this candidate’s original contribution and how long did it take?

P1
Strengthen
The system behind the brand
The case showcases identity, typography and color. The docs/package contain more system depth than the narrative exposes.

Strengthen

P1
Missing
Observed designer and developer use

Strengthen
Accessibility evidence for components

Migration or adoption value

AI output quality demonstrated

areas.name: Voicy
areas.strength: Strong interaction choreography, preview-before-insert and clear Arabic/English and privacy boundaries.
areas.reaction: This is a promising focused interaction case. I need evidence that invisible activation and safe insertion work for real users.
areas.gap: The state model is explained, but discovery, error recovery and comparative task evidence are not demonstrated.
areas.placement: Potential strong interaction-design case after a user-tested native walkthrough.
rows: P1
Missing
A primary writing workflow
The product is a general speech-to-writing layer with multiple transformations.
Who benefits most and in which application context?
Choose the actual initial audience and recurring writing task. Explain why existing dictation/editing workflows are insufficient.
The key flow is grounded in a bounded user/context rather than a universal productivity promise.
Research
P1
Strengthen
Discoverability of invisible activation
At rest there are no visible pixels, with a 52×8-point hotspot, menu bar and shortcut.
How will a new or occasional user find and remember it?
Evaluate first-run teaching, shortcut recall and an accessible menu-bar alternative. Show the tradeoff between invisibility and retrieval.
New users can invoke Voicy unaided after onboarding and understand how to return later.
Research
P1
Missing
A current native interaction recording
The case explains four states and illustrates them, without a complete native task recording.
Does the expansion preserve focus in an actual app?
Record activate, speak, release, review, edit and insert into a real target. Include keyboard-only use and visible focus context.
The recording demonstrates the claimed flow and identifies build/release status.
Design
P1
Strengthen
Permission and shortcut setup
Global input, microphone capture and insertion have platform dependencies that the case only summarizes.
Can users understand setup and recover if permission is denied?
Show permission timing, denial recovery, shortcut conflict and an alternate activation path. Explain why each permission is needed at the moment.
The first useful task remains understandable through setup failures.
Design
P1
Strengthen
Insertion uncertainty visible in UI
The architecture revalidates targets and avoids automatic retries.
What does a person see if the target changed or insertion is uncertain?
Show target-changed, no-target, insertion-uncertain and recover-to-copy states. Preserve the user’s text and explain the next safe action.
A reviewer can see how duplication and lost text are prevented in the interface.
Design
P1
Missing
Recognition and transformation recovery
The happy path turns a transcript into polished text.
Can users fix incorrect names or an unsuitable rewrite without starting over?
Demonstrate transcript correction, original-versus-transformed comparison, unsupported action and provider failure.
The user can preserve meaning, recover the original text and choose an alternative.
Design
P1
Strengthen
Arabic and mixed-language evidence
English and Arabic are described as first-class, including technical-token preservation.
Does this handle the difficult bilingual cases?
Evaluate real mixed-language dictation with names, numerals, punctuation and technical terms. Show directionality and editing behavior.
The case shows actual examples, observed errors and corrections without implying universal accuracy.

Is the workflow faster or easier than typing or standard dictation?
Compare relevant writing tasks, including review/correction time and meaning preservation, with users’ existing approach.
The evidence includes corrections and failure costs as well as successful generation.
